pill.desc: clear, colorless to pale yellow solution in a pre-filled syringe

clues.kinetics: Given into the eye for local effect; free drug in plasma is undetectable two weeks after dosing. It is cleared by target-mediated binding to free VEGF and by proteolysis.
clues.substance: Made in recombinant Chinese hamster ovary cells as a dimeric glycoprotein with a total mass of 115 kDa, supplied as a sterile, aqueous solution for intravitreal injection.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA as a single-dose pre-filled syringe or vial, given every 4 weeks at first and then every 8 weeks.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated with ocular or periocular infection, active intraocular inflammation or hypersensitivity. Conjunctival hemorrhage and eye pain are among the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Wet age-related macular degeneration, macular edema after retinal vein occlusion, diabetic macular edema and retinopathy, and retinopathy of prematurity.
clues.mechanism: Acts as a soluble decoy receptor that binds VEGF-A and PlGF, preventing their activation of VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 on endothelial cells.

tell: A recombinant decoy receptor injected into the eye that traps VEGF-A and PlGF, made in CHO cells.

evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The terminal elimination half-life (t1/2) of free aflibercept in plasma was approximately 5 to 6 days
evidence.pk.cmax: the mean C max of free aflibercept in the plasma was 0.02 mcg/mL
evidence.pill: a clear, colorless to pale yellow solution
clues.kinetics: EYLEA is administered intravitreally to exert local effects in the eye
The free aflibercept plasma concentrations were undetectable two weeks post-dosing in all patients
Aflibercept is expected to undergo elimination through both target-mediated disposition via binding to free endogenous VEGF and metabolism via proteolysis
Aflibercept is a therapeutic protein and no drug metabolism studies have been conducted
clues.substance: Aflibercept is produced in recombinant Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells
supplied as a sterile, aqueous solution for intravitreal injection
clues.product: single-dose pre-filled glass syringe or a single-dose glass vial
every 4 weeks (approximately every 28 days, monthly) for the first 3 months, followed by 2 mg (0.05 mL of 40 mg/mL solution) via intravitreal injection once every 8 weeks
clues.safety: The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) reported in patients receiving EYLEA were conjunctival hemorrhage, eye pain
clues.indication: Macular Edema Following Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO)
clues.mechanism: Aflibercept acts as a soluble decoy receptor that binds VEGF-A and PlGF, and thereby can inhibit the binding and activation of these cognate VEGF receptors
VEGF acts via two receptor tyrosine kinases, VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2
